C0.quote: We study committee voting rules under ranked preferences

C1.quote: Even for weak preferences, the SCR rule is committee monotone
C1.note: AL for the polynomial-time result (Prop. 5.4). The Theorem 8.3 swap-distance bounds are treated as part of the axiomatic and proportionality analysis.

C2.1.value: preference profile; (weak) preference relation; ranking profile
C2.1.quote: A preference profile 𝑅 is the collection of the voters’ preferences

C2.2.quote: reports a (weak) preference relation ≿𝑖 over the candidates
C2.2.note: OTH: truncated strict preferences in Sec. 6. Approval votes are mentioned only as a special case of weak orders, not as a separate input format.

C2.3.quote: runs in polynomial time if the voters have strict preferences
C2.3.note: Preferences are attributed to voters, but they are not defined separately from what is reported.

C2.4.quote: We assume that every voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 reports a (weak) preference relation
C2.4.note: The word 'reports' is used, but no distinction or relation between reported and held preferences is stated. The input is treated as the voters' preferences.

C4.1.quote: count the candidate as contributing to the satisfaction of 𝑁 ′
C4.1.note: Satisfaction of voter coalitions is defined via periphery membership in the input. No utilities are used otherwise.

C4.2.quote: on the domain of approval votes (dichotomous preferences)

C5.1.quote: we introduce our central fairness concept called proportionality for solid coalitions
C5.1.note: PSC and IPSC are proportionality and representation guarantees for voter groups.

C5.2.quote: solid coalitions 𝑁 ′ supporting a set 𝐶 ′
C5.2.note: Evaluated on the profile, with no statement relating it to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: every voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 reports a (weak) preference relation

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: this makes STV unsuitable for many applications of proportionally representative voting
majoritarian and thus not appropriate when proportionality is desired

C9.1.note: The third claim refers to the Theorem 8.3 bounds and is restated as motivation in Sec. 8.

C9.2.note: Claims about fair representation of voters and which rules to use require that the reported rankings reflect voters' actual preferences. This relation is not stated.

C2.2.reason: The formal inputs are strict rankings, weak orders and truncated rankings (OTH); approval appears only as a special case of weak orders, so APPR is not a separate format.

C4.1.reason: The paper uses 'satisfaction' for voter coalitions, which meets the applicability condition, and defines it directly in terms of the submitted preferences.

C4.2.reason: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is used, so NA does not apply, and the paper does not say what the two classes represent.

C6.VOT.reason: Voters take a fixed action in the model (they report preferences), so they are present under the codebook's 'strategically or fixed' rule, and they are non-strategic.
